title: A valid replacement canonical database still produces the safe-to-delete warning
impact: The warning can tell a user to delete the only database that still contains the migrated records.
smallestFix: Store a migration lineage marker containing the source fingerprint inside the canonical database and require that marker before warning. Treat the sidecar as advisory, not proof.

title: Renaming or moving a workspace silently selects a new empty database
impact: Tasks and memories appear to disappear after a normal directory move while the old database remains stranded under its previous path hash.
smallestFix: Create a stable workspace UUID in project metadata and key XDG storage by that UUID. Add one-time adoption from the current path-hash directory.

title: Backups become unrestorable after an application version bump
impact: A backup created by one Continuum release is rejected by the next release even when its SQLite schema and checksum are valid.
smallestFix: Make createdByVersion informational. Validate migration metadata and schema compatibility, then migrate a staged restored copy forward before publication.

title: A crash after destination migration but before receipt publication leaves an unrecoverable conflict
impact: The safe migration path can strand a valid migrated destination and force manual reconciliation after process or power loss.
smallestFix: Migrate and mark a staged database first, fsync file and parent directory, atomically publish it, and make restart adoption inspect the embedded marker.

title: The new storage and backup subsystems bypass the Effect architecture
impact: The branch now has schema-backed typed Effect failures for memory and a separate throw-based, synchronous architecture for its newest I/O-heavy features. Error rendering collapses backup failures to UNKNOWN_ERROR.
smallestFix: Parse backup contracts with Effect Schema, model expected storage/R2 failures as tagged errors, wrap Wrangler in an adapter service, and expose named Effect operations while keeping pure key and manifest functions ordinary.

title: Effect Config adoption unwraps secrets early and silently swallows file errors
impact: Redacted credentials become plain strings before the HTTP boundary, and malformed or unreadable config files become defaults without a typed diagnostic.
smallestFix: Keep API keys Redacted through MemoryConfig and unwrap only in the LLM adapter. Decode YAML through a named Effect with a typed configuration error; default only when the file is absent.

title: The real Wrangler adapter and backup CLI have thin automated coverage
impact: The in-memory protocol tests are strong, but command arguments, missing-object classification, environment handling, and CLI rendering rely mostly on one manual acceptance run.
smallestFix: Test the adapter against a fake executable that records argv and returns representative Wrangler failures. Add credential-free CLI tests for configure, create, list, restore, and JSON errors.

title: Manual boundary parsing and unused exports add avoidable surface
evidence: Knip: backupConfigPath, BACKUP_FORMAT_VERSION, BACKUP_OBJECT_PREFIX, projectPrefix, generationPrefix
impact: The branch adds 24 net anti-slop diagnostics, mostly unknown dictionaries and runtime type checks, plus five exports with no production consumer.
smallestFix: Use Effect Schema for remote/config/receipt boundaries and keep path helpers/constants private unless another module owns a real use.

title: Committed design docs contain machine-specific operational names
impact: Library documentation now names a personal host bucket and an unrelated bucket, which does not help other installations and couples docs to one acceptance run.
smallestFix: Use placeholders in product documentation and keep the concrete acceptance bucket in an ignored local run record.

title: Cloud support is manual backup, not automatic synchronization
impact: The branch delivers a sound recovery primitive but no timer, write hook, freshness status, or multi-machine sync. Users can easily assume backup is current when it is not.
smallestFix: Keep the one-writer protocol, but add explicit backup status/freshness and an optional systemd timer setup. Continue to defer bidirectional merge semantics.
